ui.recheck: Things are changing by the hour. Check again before you leave.
ui.not_endorsed: No organisation listed here has endorsed this guide. No number is guaranteed to connect.

s01.headline: I was at Jantar Mantar 1.0.
s01.headline2: If you’re going for 2.0, here’s what I want you to know.
s01.deck: Preparation, safety, documentation, and looking after each other.

s02.headline: Before you leave, know what’s changed.
s02.foot: The protest does not have police permission. Going is your decision. Make it with current information.

s03.headline: Your phone may stop connecting. Prepare before it does.
s03.testimony: At Jantar Mantar 1.0 in July, communication was a real problem for me, and I found 112 unreliable.
s03.confirmed: Mobile internet is reported suspended within about 4 km of Jantar Mantar until 10 pm on 10 Oct.
s03.unverified: Claims that calls will be jammed have not been verified. Plan as if they might be.
steps: Download this guide and any maps while you’re still connected.
Write key numbers on paper. Keep it in a pocket, not your bag.
Charge your phone fully and carry a power bank.
Tell family you may be unreachable for hours.
Agree a check-in time and a meeting point.
Carry cash. UPI and cab apps need data.
Know how you’ll get home without an app.

s04.headline: A few small things can make a difficult day easier.
items: Water
More than you think you need
Light food
Something that won’t spoil
ORS or electrolytes
If they suit you
Your medicines
Prescriptions, inhalers, anything you rely on
Power bank and cable
Charged the night before
Comfortable shoes
You may walk far
Clothes for the weather
Sun, heat, or rain
Identification
Basic ID only
Small cash
For water, food, a ride home
Numbers on paper
Family, a friend, legal aid
Your access needs
Mobility aids, personal care, sanitary supplies
s04.note: Don’t go without medicine, care or support you need to be there. No protest is worth that.

s05.headline: You may arrive alone. You don’t have to feel alone.
body: Talk to the people around you. Ask where they’ve come from and listen to the answer.
If someone looks lost or overwhelmed, check on them, gently. Share water, a charger, the information you have.
Swap numbers if you both want to. Stay near people you trust, and check on each other through the day.
s05.boundary_label: Friendly is not the same as trusting.
s05.boundary: You don’t owe anyone your number, your address or your company. Don’t go somewhere with a stranger. Leave anything that feels wrong.
s05.close: People who were strangers in the morning can still choose to look out for each other.

s06.headline: If something goes wrong, know who to contact.
s06.medical: Serious injury needs qualified emergency care. Don’t attempt improvised treatment in a crowd.

s07.headline: Know your rights. Know where to get help.
rows: Calmly ask: Am I free to go, am I being detained, or am I under arrest?
If you’re arrested, police must tell you the grounds and the offence. BNSS s. 47
Police must inform a person you name about your arrest and where you’re held. BNSS s. 48
You may meet a lawyer of your choice during interrogation. BNSS s. 38
For a bailable offence, you must be told you can be released on bail. BNSS s. 47(2)
An arrested person must be produced before a magistrate within 24 hours. Constitution, Art. 22(2)
s07.conduct: Stay calm. Don’t resist or argue. Note names, badge numbers and the place. Ask for legal aid.
s07.disclaimer: General information, not legal advice. How these rules apply depends on the situation. Speak to a lawyer.

s08.headline: Help doesn’t always come with a uniform.
s08.honest: As of 9 Oct, 9:40 pm, I have not been able to confirm any independent lawyer, doctor or volunteer who will be on the ground on 10 Oct.
s08.template_note: If you’re a lawyer, doctor or volunteer who will be there, message me. I’ll verify you and add you, with your consent.

s09.headline: Record what happens. Preserve what you record.

cols.label: Record
items: Film from a safe distance.
Never obstruct police or medics.
Capture what happens before and after, not only the peak.
Say or note the date, time and place.
Note names, badge numbers, vehicle numbers if visible.

cols.label: Preserve
items: Keep the original file, with sound.
Don’t trim or filter the original.
Back it up to a second place when you can.
Don’t rely on clips you’ve posted.

cols.label: Publish with care
items: Think about faces of people who could be harmed.
Share with a lawyer before posting, if it may be evidence.

s09.impersonation: If someone claiming authority seems suspicious, don’t confront them or assume from appearance. Note what you can and verify through official or legal channels later.
s09.close: A complete record can matter long after the moment has passed.

s10.headline: What if you can’t reach someone?
steps: Go to the time and place you agreed. Phones may simply be down.
Someone who was with them may know where they went.
Try a plain call or SMS
These may work where data doesn’t.
Call legal aid: 15100. Note when and where they were last seen.
If you think they’re in danger
Use emergency services, and seek help in person only if it’s safe.
s10.dont: Don’t post unverified ‘missing’ claims. Don’t share their phone number, address or photos publicly without thinking about their safety.
s10.note112: 112 is the official emergency number. I found it unreliable at 1.0, so keep other routes ready.

s11.headline: You don’t have to be there to be useful.
items: Follow reliable updates and pass on only what’s verified.
Help a friend make sense of the transport changes.
Save the contacts in this guide and share them.
Check on people you know who are going.
Correct misinformation, calmly and with a source.
Support legal-aid and rights groups through their official channels.
Follow what happens after the day, in court and in public.
s11.civic: electoralsearch.eci.gov.in · Voter helpline 1950 (Election Commission of India)

s12.headline: I hope everyone gets home safe.
s12.body: Whatever you decide about tomorrow, decide it with good information. If you go, go prepared. Look after yourself, and look after the person next to you. Keep your records. And if someone needs help afterwards, don’t let them carry it alone.

1.headline: I was at Jantar Mantar 1.0 in July.
1.body: If you’re thinking of going for 2.0 on 10 Oct, I’ve put together what I wish I’d known: how to prepare for losing signal, who to contact, how to record what happens, and how to look after each other.
1.cta: Full guide on my profile. Save it while you have signal.

2.headline: Do these tonight.
items: Download this guide and maps.
Write key numbers on paper.
Charge your phone and power bank.
Tell family you may be unreachable.
Agree a check-in time and place.
Carry cash for food and a ride home.

4.headline: Help doesn’t always come with a uniform.
4.body: I haven’t yet been able to confirm independent lawyers, doctors or volunteers on the ground for 10 Oct. If you’re one of them, message me. I’ll verify you and add you, with your consent.
